problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13947863/assets/faa8a8e0521972fa860d474ac079405b6930df6c47fda05808fdf242d6d6922b.png)

The equation $xy=5$ represents a hyperbola. The tangent line at the point $(1,5)$ on the hyperbola intersects the $y$-axis at the point $P.$ What are the coordinates of $P?$
worked_solution:
First of all, we need to find the slope of the tangent line at the point $(1,5).$

To find the slope of the tangent line, we will calculate the derivative using implicit differentiation, assuming that $y=y(x).$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(xy) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5) \\ x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+y & =0 \\ x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-y \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{-y}{x} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-\frac{y}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the slope of the tangent at the point $(1,\,5)$  is 

$$
\begin{aligned}m & ={(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x})}_{(1,\,5)} \\  & ={(-\frac{y}{x})}_{(1,\,5)} \\  & =-\frac{5}{1} \\  & =-5.\end{aligned}
$$

We can write the equation of the tangent at the point $(1,\,5)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-{y}_{1}) & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ (y-5) & =-5(x-1) \\ y & =-5(x-1)+5 \\ y & =-5x+10\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we just need to find where this tangent line intersects the $y$-axis. At the point $P$ the $x$-coordinate is $0,$ so we set $x=0$ and solve for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-5x+10 \\ y & =-5\cdot 0+10 \\ y & =10\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of $P$ are $(0,\,10).$

The equation xy=5 represents a hyperbola. The tangent line at the point (1,5) on the hyperbola intersects the y-axis at the point P. What are the coordinates of P?

a
 (0,15)
b
 (0,12)
c
 (0,9)
d
(0,14)
e
(0,10)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First of all, we need to find the slope of the tangent line at the point (1,5).

To find the slope of the tangent line, we will calculate the derivative using implicit differentiation, assuming that y=y(x).

ddx(xy)=ddx(5)xdydx+y=0xdydx=−ydydx=−yxdydx=−yx So, the slope of the tangent at the point (1,5) is

m=(dydx)(1,5)=(−yx)(1,5)=−51=−5. We can write the equation of the tangent at the point (1,5) as follows:

(y−y1)=m(x−x1)(y−5)=−5(x−1)y=−5(x−1)+5y=−5x+10

Now, we just need to find where this tangent line intersects the y-axis. At the point P the x-coordinate is 0, so we set x=0 and solve for y:

y=−5x+10y=−5⋅0+10y=10 Therefore, the coordinates of P are (0,10).
